newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki puts on late spurt, pointers turn bullish.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki puts on late spurt, pointers turn bullish.

text.p: Finnish shares were higher all day and extended gains in a late spurt as Wall Street opened higher, the Finnish market particularly cheered by strength in paper stocks and technology shares, brokers said.

With the technical 1,000-point resistance level in the FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark breached, brokers said all the short-term pointers had turned healthy, pushing rate hike fears in the U.S. onto the backburner for now.
"It's all good at the moment," said one, pointing at Nokia's gains on IBM's Q1 report, Stora's better-than-expected Q1 report, and a paper stock upgrade from Morgan Stanley.

The HEX general index ended up 1.15 percent at 2,884.31 -- its session high -- and the FOX index closed up 1.4 percent at 1,008.50 points, partly on demand for blue chips but also helped by a futures expiry which came with many investors short.

Another saw a global "run for quality" boosting blue chips and said in Finland "someone seems to be hauling in UPM". UPM, recently boosted by speculation it may buy all or part of Canada's Repap, closed up 5.00 markka at 120.00, its highest since March 7; and topped volumes at 22 percent of the total.

Bourse newcomer Nordic Aluminium NOA1V.HE started at 55.00 markka and then retreated to about 53.50, and brokers said the 50.00 markka offering looked well priced. The stock ended at its 55 markka high, 7.60 percent above the issue price.

Media group Aamulehti trimmed strong gains of earlier this week on its merger with TV broadcaster MTV -- it fell 7.00 markka or almost four percent to 187.00, but was still well above the 155 level where it traded before the news.
"It looks like the big euphoria is over," one broker said. "Investors have noticed that the MTV merger is quite expensive for Aamulehti," said another.

Steel group Rautaruukki rose 0.70 markka to 44.00 after a slightly better-than-expected earnings report from Swedish steel group SSAB but brokers said the gains were capped by the Finnish group's issue plans and trade was modest.
Pipe and furniture group Asko added 0.50 markka to 91.00 in fairly hefty volume on a second consecutive day of big trades brokered in-house at Evli Securities.
